research_concepts: counter-strategy lift (PULL_UP PPP conditional on PNR failure)
unit-level consistency (share of units with lift > 0, median lift > 2pp)
methodological_questions: How is 'PNR fail' operationalized from play-by-play, and is it defined independently of the points outcome used to measure PULL_UP lift?
What is the unit (team-season, team-game, or matchup) for the '>=70% of units' criterion, and how many units exist?
Is PULL_UP lift measured against a matched baseline (PULL_UP after non-failed PnR, or PULL_UP in the same team-season) rather than against league average?
Do the four retrieved records provide any direct test of this counter claim, or only adjacent descriptive checks?

historical_evidence.finding: Holdout play-type rank validation (LAYER_AUDIT): pre-game play-type PPP ranking from training data correlated with held-out efficiency (median rho +0.539; 88.4% rho>0; top-3 median hit 100%; median lift +0.4261 PPP). The record's own failure mechanism is coded C_artifact, with the doc caveat that top-3 lift partly reflects league-wide high-efficiency play types (CUT, PUTBACK, TRANSITION) and that 10.5% of rows mislead (rho<0). Sample: 908 game-team rows, 454 games. Related family FAM:SF-APPA-035 was named but not returned.

Shot-level PNR rates from play-by-play, 2024-25 half-court shots, 30 teams (roughly 5994-6581 shots per team). Shares range from about 7.6% (OKC) to 13.8% (IND). The rates are a calibration input for PBPProxyPNR, with later logs showing calibrated PNR around 17.9-19.6% of possessions. Verdict: descriptive; no validation recorded.

Defensive PPP allowed and possession share, RS vs playoffs, 25 teams, minimum 30 possessions per cell. PNR share rose +12.1pp in playoffs, with PNR PPP change -0.139 and PULL_UP PPP change +0.341. No inferential test was run. The record notes the PNR share jump may reflect tagging differences.

TOV_FORCE matchup decomposition on four playoff games. Team-PT lifts were small and sign-mixed (for example POR vs SAS PNR -4.1pp). Player-channel lifts were large but based on small cells (for example Banchero on Huerter SPOT_UP +8.4pp, n_def=17, n_off=54). The record says primary-defender attribution includes helper steals and that there was no holdout or outcome check.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Ranking play types by PPP and reading top-ranked play-type lift as evidence of a specific counter or edge.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as C_artifact: top-3 lift partly reflects league-wide high-efficiency play types, so the lift does not isolate a PNR-specific counter. Mislead rate of 10.5% (rho<0). Auto-tagged DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using shot-level PNR rates from play-by-play as a label/proxy for possession-level PNR.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as E_unclear with no validation recorded. The record notes that possession-level rates are expected to be higher, so the shot-level proxy is not the same construct as the possession label.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Comparing play-type shares and PPP across regular season and playoffs without an inferential test.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as E_unclear with no inferential test. The +12.1pp PNR share change may reflect tagging differences (LABEL_ERROR), and the record flags MECHANICAL_FLOOR.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Player-channel matchup lift on four playoff games.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as A_unanswerable with LIM:insufficient_exposure. Cell n was often 15-28 defensive possessions (up to 54 offensive); primary-defender attribution included helper steals; no holdout or outcome check.

evidence_establishes: Play-type-level PPP is recoverable from the play-by-play-derived data for 25-30 teams across RS and playoffs, so team-level PULL_UP and PNR possession counts are plausibly available (FAM:SF-APPM-058, FAM:SF-APPS-012).
Naive play-type lift rankings are confounded by league-wide play-type efficiency, so any PULL_UP lift must be compared against a baseline of similar possessions (FAM:SF-APPA-063).
Player-level or small-cell matchup lifts are too noisy to support league-wide claims (FAM:SF-APPA-066).
PNR tagging is itself uncertain and differs between sources or contexts, so PNR-fail labels need validation (FAM:SF-APPS-012, FAM:SF-APPM-058).
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether PULL_UP PPP is higher than baseline after a failed PNR. None of the four records tests this conditional comparison.
Whether the 70%-of-units and median >2pp criterion holds. No record reports a unit-level sign or median-lift distribution for PULL_UP after PNR failure.
The correct definition of 'units' or the number of independent units.
Whether the 'supported' status of FAM:SF-APPA-063 applies to this question. That record concerns pre-game play-type ranking, not PNR-fail-to-PULL_UP lift, and it is coded as an artifact.
Any effect for the 2025-26 playoffs, which were partial as of 2026-05-23.
own_inferences: The question as posed is a conditional, league-wide consistency claim with no stated baseline. Without a defined baseline, a positive PULL_UP lift could reflect that PULL_UP is simply a high-efficiency play type.

PNR fail as defined by points-scored or turnover outcomes would make the label depend on the same outcome used to measure lift (OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL). Failure needs to be defined from defensive or pre-outcome signals.

With about 30 teams per season and 3-4 seasons, the unit count (about 90-120 team-seasons) gives limited power for a 70% sign-consistency criterion, especially with a 2pp median threshold and noisy per-unit PULL_UP sample sizes.
The retrieved records were not produced by a test of this exact hypothesis, so the historical evidence informs the design choices and risks but does not answer the question.
uncertainties: The truncated text of FAM:SF-APPA-063 and FAM:SF-APPA-066 (marked '[cut]') was not read in full. Related family FAM:SF-APPA-035 was named but not returned.
The defensive vs offensive framing of 'counter' is ambiguous. The question says PULL_UP is a counter to PNR failure, but the data's counter-strategy unit is not specified.
The number of possessions per unit for PNR-fail-then-PULL_UP sequences is unknown and may be too sparse for team-game units.
The data source's PNR and PULL_UP tagging reliability is not documented in the retrieved records; FAM:SF-APPS-012 and FAM:SF-APPM-058 suggest it varies.
Whether 'PNR fail' has a defined play-by-play event (for example turnover or no-shot outcome) is not stated.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved records showed that prior play-type analyses were either artifacts or non-hypothesis descriptive checks, that PNR labels and shares are unvalidated, and that small-cell matchup lifts are unstable. These findings moved the decision from a straightforward test to a proceed-with-changes design that requires a matched baseline, an outcome-independent PNR-fail definition, and placebo and holdout checks. The records did not make the question answerable as posed.

blocking_constraints.text: PNR-fail label must be defined without using the PULL_UP points outcome; otherwise lift is partly mechanical.
League-wide play-type efficiency and opponent/defender quality confound PULL_UP lift unless compared to matched baseline possessions.
Around 90-120 team-season units limit power for the 70% sign criterion; per-unit PULL_UP after failed PNR may be small.
PNR tagging differs across sources and contexts (FAM:SF-APPS-012), which can misassign PNR-fail possessions.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record tests PULL_UP lift conditional on PNR failure or the 70%-of-units, median >2pp criterion. The records are an artifact-coded play-type ranking check, two descriptive play-type comparisons without inferential tests, and a small four-game matchup decomposition. They inform risks and data limitations but do not answer the question.

risks.text: If PNR fail is defined from the outcome of the same possession or from points scored, the PULL_UP lift is partly built into the label.
PULL_UP may be generally efficient across the league (FAM:SF-APPA-063), so lift versus league average overstates a counter effect; shot quality, opponent, and personnel are uncontrolled.
PULL_UP frequency and PPP differ by team and season; a 2pp threshold is small relative to the base rate and sensitive to the chosen baseline.
Unit count of about 30 teams per season gives limited power for a 70% consistency criterion; per-unit PULL_UP after failed PNR counts may be small.
Matchup-level cells can be very small (FAM:SF-APPA-066: n 15-54), so finer units would be unstable.
PNR tagging and helper-steal attribution can misassign possessions (FAM:SF-APPS-012, FAM:SF-APPA-066).
Shot-level PNR rates differ from possession-level labels (FAM:SF-APPM-058); the proxy's validity is unestablished.
Testing both the 70% and median >2pp criteria, and choosing among unit definitions after seeing results, inflates false positives.
Pooling 2022-23 through 2025-26 may mix play-type trends across seasons; the 2025-26 playoffs were partial as of 2026-05-23.
Without a placebo condition, a positive lift may reflect general play-type efficiency rather than the PNR-fail sequence.
Possession sequencing from the play-by-play (PNR -> PULL_UP ordering, possession boundaries) is error-prone and must be validated.

design.estimand: Within each unit, the difference in points per possession (pp) between PULL_UP possessions that follow a failed PNR (defined from pre-outcome signals) and matched PULL_UP possessions that do not follow a failed PNR, summarised across units.
design.unit: Team-season (offense or defense as specified in advance, with counter role defined explicitly). Team-game units are a secondary check only if counts allow.
design.sample: Regular seasons 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25 and 2025-26 (complete from 2026-04-13). Playoffs 2022-23 to 2024-25 only; 2025-26 playoffs excluded because they were partial as of 2026-05-23.
design.power: Pre-compute per-unit PULL_UP after failed PNR counts. Require a minimum count per unit (for example 30 possessions per condition) and report the number of units retained. Simulate power for the 70% sign criterion over the retained units before analysis; if power is inadequate, report the test as inconclusive rather than underpowered.
design.controls: Match on play-type context and shot distance, period, score margin, and team-season; control for initiator and primary-defender identity via mixed-effects or stratified estimates; use rotation and matchup data to adjust for personnel where available; exclude possessions with substitutions or helper-steal attribution issues.
design.falsification: Placebo PNR-fail defined from non-PNR sequences with the same shape; label shuffling within team-season (expected lift near zero); holdout season or playoff check for consistency of sign; pre-registered sensitivity to alternative PNR-fail definitions.
design.multiplicity: Pre-specify one primary test (share of units with positive lift, plus median lift with bootstrap CI). Treat the 2pp threshold and unit definitions as fixed in advance; report all other variants as exploratory.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if (a) the share of retained units with positive lift is at least 70% with a one-sided lower confidence bound above 50%, (b) the median lift is above 2pp with a bootstrap CI excluding 2pp from below, and (c) placebo and label-shuffle lifts are near zero. Rejected if the share or median criterion fails with adequate power. Otherwise report as uncertain.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game play-by-play, substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, and box-score summary for 2022-23 to 2024-25 (RS and playoffs) and 2025-26 RS (complete from 2026-04-13). Graph-derived play-type possession records must be rebuilt from the same play-by-play snapshot and versioned; 2025-26 playoff rows excluded.

methodological_questions: Does PULL_UP possession points lift exceed 0 in at least 70% of units when PnR fails?
What unit definition and lift threshold (median lift >2pp) are appropriate for a league-wide counter claim?
How should selection, base rate and label derivation risks be handled in play-type counter tests?
args.query: PNR fail then PULL_UP counter lift league-wide units median lift 2pp defensive suppression counter strategy

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 4 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
